title: raven rtr monitor NDJSON, schema_version 1
description: One NDJSON line: one record. The record type is event_type. See docs/reference/telemetry-ndjson.md. Within schema_version 1 changes are additive only; consumers must ignore fields and record types they do not know. This schema lists exactly what version 1 emits, and is strict (additionalProperties false) so that RAVEN's own tests catch drift: a consumer validating with it must allow for additions.

connected.description: A TCP (or TLS) connection to the cache was opened and the first query is about to be sent.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract. Records written before it existed have none.

timestamp.description: When the event happened: RFC 3339 with up to nanosecond precision and a UTC offset, which consumers must honor. RAVEN writes UTC (Z); files from older releases may carry the host's local offset.

cache.description: The RTR cache, as given to --cache (host:port).

event_type.description: A TCP (or TLS) connection to the cache was opened and the first query is about to be sent.

proto_version.description: RTR protocol version of the session (on connected and version_downgrade: the version asked for). 0 carries no ASPA.

disconnected.description: A session that connected has ended. Exactly one per connected.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract. Records written before it existed have none.

timestamp.description: When the event happened: RFC 3339 with up to nanosecond precision and a UTC offset, which consumers must honor. RAVEN writes UTC (Z); files from older releases may carry the host's local offset.

cache.description: The RTR cache, as given to --cache (host:port).

event_type.description: A sync completed: the cache sent End of Data.

proto_version.description: RTR protocol version of the session (on connected and version_downgrade: the version asked for). 0 carries no ASPA.

serial.description: The cache's serial from End of Data. Always present, 0 included (older files omit it when 0).

serial_changed.description: The serial differs from the previous sync's (true on the first).

vrp_total.description: Distinct VRPs this cache holds after the sync (a VRP announced twice counts once). Always present, 0 included.

vrp_announced.description: VRP announcement PDUs received in this sync, re-announcements included. Always present, 0 included.

vrp_withdrawn.description: VRP withdrawal PDUs received in this sync. Always present, 0 included.

vrp_added.description: VRPs this cache came to hold in this sync: the net change, not the PDUs (a re-announcement of a held VRP adds none). A full sync counts against the cache's data before it. Always present, 0 included, in records from RAVENs that write it; absent in older ones.

vrp_removed.description: VRPs this cache stopped holding in this sync: the net change, not the PDUs. A full sync counts against the cache's data before it. Always present, 0 included, in records from RAVENs that write it; absent in older ones.

aspa_total.description: ASPA records (customer ASes) held after the sync. Always present, 0 included.

aspa_announced.description: ASPA announcement PDUs in this sync. Always present, 0 included.

aspa_withdrawn.description: ASPA withdrawal PDUs in this sync. Always present, 0 included.

aspa_added.description: Customer ASes this cache came to hold an ASPA record for in this sync: the net change (a provider-set replacement is neither added nor removed). A full sync counts against the cache's data before it. Always present, 0 included, in records from RAVENs that write it; absent in older ones.

aspa_removed.description: Customer ASes whose ASPA record this cache stopped holding in this sync: the net change. A full sync counts against the cache's data before it. Always present, 0 included, in records from RAVENs that write it; absent in older ones.

sync_duration_ns.description: Nanoseconds from sending the query to receiving End of Data. Always present.

interval_since_ns.description: Nanoseconds since the previous sync's End of Data in this process. Absent on the first sync and when 0.

data_fingerprint.description: The cache's data set as of this sync, VRPs and ASPA records, as an order-independent fingerprint: 32 hex digits, equal for equal sets whatever order or session they came in. Staleness and data_regressed compare these, not serials. Absent from records of RAVENs before it.

error.description: The cache sent an Error Report that is a fault: any code but 2, and code 4 on an established session, at version 0 or at a pinned version; the session ends. Or, with error_origin client, RAVEN found a protocol error in what the cache sent during a sync (code 7: a record announced again while held; code 6: a record withdrawn that was not held). RAVEN keeps a count per record, so the cache's intended state holds, and resyncs with a Reset Query on the same session; the session goes on.

cache_not_ready.description: The cache sent Error Report code 2 (No Data Available): it is still starting. Not a fault; retried at the same version.

trigger.description: structural: cache_reset, error_report, protocol_error (an error with error_origin client), data_stale (with a stale record) or data_regressed (with a data_regressed record). statistical: the metric that tripped the hard threshold, or the metrics that crossed the soft threshold joined with + (a correlated trip).

severity.description: high: structural, or a hard threshold. medium: a correlated trip.

z_scores.description: Statistical only: modified z (unitless) of each metric at or above its soft threshold.

raw.description: Statistical only: every metric's value in the sync (ns for *_ns, counts otherwise).

divergence.description: The cache has persistently disagreed with the other compared caches (longer than the settle window): a divergence episode began. One per episode, not per item.

timestamp.description: When the event happened: RFC 3339 with up to nanosecond precision and a UTC offset, which consumers must honor. RAVEN writes UTC (Z); files from older releases may carry the host's local offset.

episode.description: The episode's number at this cache, from 1, in this process.

started_at.description: When the episode's earliest difference first appeared, in its current shape (the compared caches and who held it).

compared.description: The caches compared when the record was written, in --cache order: those connected that have completed a sync in their current session.

settle_ns.description: The settle window in effect, in nanoseconds: a difference counts once it has lasted longer.

counts.description: Persistent differences attributed to the cache, by kind; only kinds with at least one.

samples.description: Up to 20 of the persistent differences, taken from each kind in turn, sorted by kind and item.

prefix.description: The VRP's prefix, as the cache sent it (address/length).

providers.description: ASPA kinds: the cache's provider set, sorted; absent when it has none.

majority_providers.description: ASPA kinds: the majority's provider set, sorted; absent on aspa_split and when the majority has none.

agree.description: The compared caches that hold what this cache holds for the item, it included.

disagree.description: The compared caches that do not.

split_with.description: When counts has a split kind: the caches on the other side of the split items.

divergence_resolved.description: A divergence episode ended: the cache no longer disagrees with the other compared caches on anything.

timestamp.description: When the event happened: RFC 3339 with up to nanosecond precision and a UTC offset, which consumers must honor. RAVEN writes UTC (Z); files from older releases may carry the host's local offset.

cache.description: The cache whose sync completed the match, as given to --cache (host:port).

caches.description: The caches the change reached: every compared cache, in --cache order.

changes.description: Each cache's sync that carried the change, in --cache order.

overlap.description: The least overlap between the completing cache's change and another's: shared items over the larger change's items.

settle_ns.description: The settle window in effect, in nanoseconds: a difference counts once it has lasted longer.

samples.description: Up to 20 items every cache's change has, taken from each kind of change in turn.

prefix.description: The VRP's prefix, as the cache sent it (address/length).

stale.description: A stale episode began: the cache's data (VRPs and ASPA records) has not changed for longer than its threshold, whether it goes on syncing or not; checked at every sync and every 15 seconds. One record per episode.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract. Records written before it existed have none.

timestamp.description: When the event happened: RFC 3339 with up to nanosecond precision and a UTC offset, which consumers must honor. RAVEN writes UTC (Z); files from older releases may carry the host's local offset.

event_type.description: A stale episode began: the cache's data (VRPs and ASPA records) has not changed for longer than its threshold, whether it goes on syncing or not; checked at every sync and every 15 seconds. One record per episode.

serial.description: The cache's serial at detection. For information only: serials restart with every session and differ between anycast nodes.

last_change.description: When the current data set became current: its last change, or for a return to earlier data when that set was first current.

gap_ns.description: Nanoseconds from last_change to this record.

expected_gap_ns.description: The threshold gap_ns exceeded: max(4 x median, 3 x 90th percentile of this cache's gaps between data changes, 30 minutes), 4 hours before 20 gaps are known (at most 4 hours before 100), or --stale-threshold.

syncs_without_change.description: Syncs since the last data change that saw no change.

threshold_source.description: Where expected_gap_ns came from: learned from the gaps, the 4-hour default (fewer than 20 gaps known, or a learned threshold above it with fewer than 100), or --stale-threshold.

gaps_learned.description: How many gaps between data changes the threshold had to learn from (at most 500).

scope.description: With several --cache only: upstream if every compared cache went stale within the settle window, local if not. The record is held until that is known, at most the settle window. Absent with one cache.

cache_state.description: The cache's connection state when the episode began. connected: the cache answers, serving data that does not change. disconnected: the cache cannot be reached (no session) while its last data, still in use, ages. A disconnected cache that reconnects with the same data stays in the episode.

stale_resolved.description: A stale episode ended: the cache's data changed. A return to earlier data does not end one.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract. Records written before it existed have none.

timestamp.description: When the event happened: RFC 3339 with up to nanosecond precision and a UTC offset, which consumers must honor. RAVEN writes UTC (Z); files from older releases may carry the host's local offset.

event_type.description: A stale episode ended: the cache's data changed. A return to earlier data does not end one.

stale_since.description: When the stale record was written.

duration_ns.description: Nanoseconds from stale_since to this record: how long the episode lasted.

last_change.description: When the data that went stale became current.

gap_ns.description: Nanoseconds from last_change to this record: how long the data went unchanged.

sync_type.description: The type of the sync that changed the data.

resolution.description: How the episode ended. data_change: the data changed within a session. reconnect_new_data: the first sync after a reconnect brought new data. A reconnect to the same data does not end an episode.

vrp_added.description: That sync's net change, as on its sync record.

vrp_removed.description: That sync's net change, as on its sync record.

aspa_added.description: That sync's net change, as on its sync record.

aspa_removed.description: That sync's net change, as on its sync record.

data_regressed.description: The cache returned to a data set it served earlier (among its last 50, none current more than 7 days ago), inside a session or after a reconnect: a lagging anycast node, say. Only a significant return: that set was current in all, or has been gone, for longer than the stale threshold; a briefer one is churn, a data change. Not a data change: the staleness clock runs from when that set was first current.
